audit_findings.title: Unreserved litigation exposure sits outside the equity bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: An uninsured settlement, damages award, disgorgement, or injunction would reduce the cash bridge, future OE, or growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is currently unable to predict the outcome of the lawsuit and is unable to reasonably estimate the amount or range of loss, if any, that could result from an unfavorable outcome.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved valuation exposure, not a demonstrated bridge error. The June 2026 10-Q says the OpenEvidence case was stayed for mediation, no material loss contingency was recorded, and the company could not estimate any settlement or unfavorable-outcome loss. The requested remedies could affect value, but the record supplies neither a loss range nor insurance coverage sufficient to establish materiality against $687.789 million of cash and short-term investments.
audit_findings.action: Obtain policy limits and exclusions, indemnification terms, mediation or post-quarter developments, and counsel's probability-weighted loss range; rerun the bridge and operating scenarios for any uninsured amount or injunction-related OE impact.

audit_findings.title: Live litigation costs may have been stripped as one-offs
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.853 million pre-tax, equal to 2.7% of $179.2 million anchor OE; a conservative dollar-for-dollar recurring reduction would lower value by about $0.27-$0.38 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If added back, recurring defense costs inflate sustainable anchor OE and therefore operating PV.
audit_findings.evidence: The court denied the motions to dismiss as to all other claims, including all counterclaims asserted by Doximity, and the litigation is proceeding.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the FY2026 OE bridge added back these expenses is unresolved, but the filed amount bounds the identified issue. Treating the entire $4.853 million as a perpetual dollar-for-dollar OE reduction would reduce bear, base, and bull operating values by approximately $57.7 million, $68.2 million, and $80.5 million, or $0.27, $0.32, and $0.38 per share. Even the bull value would remain about $17.02 versus the $26.35 market price, so this item alone cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $4.853 million legal-expense line through the FY2026 OE bridge; if added back, rerun OE with a normalized recurring legal-cost deduction until the proceedings end.

audit_findings.title: Recurring software development investment may be understated
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.6 million capitalized in FY2026 versus $7.4 million amortized, a $5.2 million difference; even omitting the full $12.6 million equals 7.0% of anchor OE and about $0.71-$0.99 per share of scenario value
audit_findings.mechanism: An insufficient maintenance-capex deduction would overstate anchor OE and every projected operating cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended March 31, 2026, 2025, and 2024, the Company capitalized $ 12.6 million, $ 8.4 million, and $ 6.8 million, respectively, of internal-use software development costs, which are included in property and equipment, net on the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate how the OE bridge treated internal-use development, but the filed FY2026 amount provides a conservative scale test. If none of the full $12.6 million had been deducted, bear, base, and bull values would fall by approximately $0.71, $0.84, and $0.99 per share. The bull value would still be about $16.41 versus the $26.35 market price. The identified current-period treatment therefore cannot change the conclusion, although the growing expenditure warrants continued normalization work.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE to the $8.901 million cash development outlay and $3.633 million capitalized stock compensation comprising the filed $12.6 million total; document the maintenance portion and rerun if the existing deduction is smaller.

audit_findings.title: The zero-growth bear case omits plausible customer-loss contraction
audit_findings.magnitude: 11% of FY2026 revenue, approximately $70.9 million of $644.863 million; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Loss or repricing of a major customer would introduce negative near-term growth and potentially reduce the OE base used in the bear scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: While one customer accounted for 10% or more of total revenue for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 and no customer met this threshold for the fiscal years ended March 31, 2025 and 2024, our revenue is relatively concentrated within a small number of key customers.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking scenario risk rather than a loss presently demonstrated in the numbers. One customer represented 11% of FY2026 revenue, but no customer represented at least 10% of revenue or receivables in the June 2026 quarter, and quarterly revenue still grew 7%. Profit contribution, renewal status, and any replacement revenue are not disclosed, so the OE impact cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain customer-level renewal dates, agency exposure, pricing changes, and contribution margins; rerun a temporary and sustained customer-loss case when evidence indicates nonrenewal or material repricing is reasonably likely.

audit_findings.title: The contingent earn-out may be an omitted non-debt claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 remaining at June 30, 2026; the final $6.0 million payment was 0.19% of $3.206 billion base equity value and about $0.03 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: An outstanding acquisition earn-out would normally reduce the equity bridge, but the final payment was already reflected in the June 30 cash balance used by the valuation.
audit_findings.evidence: The contingent earn-out consideration liability relates to the AMiON acquisition, which closed on April 1, 2022.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves the uncertainty. The liability moved from $5.910 million to $6.000 million and was fully settled by a final $6.000 million payment during the June quarter, leaving no remaining obligation. Because the $687.789 million cash and short-term-investment bridge is dated June 30, after that payment, no additional deduction is required.
audit_findings.action: Retain the June 30 earn-out roll-forward and cash-flow reconciliation in the valuation workpapers; no rerun is needed unless the cash bridge predates the settlement.
